strengths: The paper addresses an important computer vision problem: distilling large image datasets without expensive bilevel optimization. Combining representative feature targets with per-class BatchNorm matching provides a practical synthesis pipeline.

The reported results are promising across three datasets and several compression levels. At 50 images per class, Table 1 reports 57.6% on ImageNet-1K versus 53.5% for CDA, and 59.4% on Tiny-ImageNet versus 48.7%. Main results include variability across three runs.
Table 2 demonstrates useful transfer across ResNet architectures. ImageNet-1K data distilled with ResNet-18 achieve 61.3% and 62.2% with ResNet-50 and ResNet-101 at 50 images per class.

The manuscript includes component ablations, regularization sensitivity, qualitative comparisons, and implementation details. It appropriately attributes the main datasets, SRe2L framework, barycenter algorithm, and POT library, and acknowledges pretrained-teacher dependence and inherited dataset biases.
weaknesses: The central novelty needs stronger justification. With one input distribution, freely optimized support weights, and squared-Euclidean cost, Eq. (7) reduces to the ordinary k-means quantization objective in feature space: each real feature assigns its mass to its nearest center. This equivalence is neither discussed nor evaluated through a k-means-target baseline using identical image-recovery losses. Consequently, the distinct contribution of the proposed Wasserstein formulation remains unclear.

The optimized distribution is not clearly preserved by the practical pipeline. Algorithm 2 returns nonuniform weights, but Algorithm 1 and Eq. (16) retain only the support locations; weighted sampling or student training is not described. Even perfect feature matching therefore need not recover the optimized empirical distribution. The solver description also needs correction: Algorithm 2 updates weights before reusing a transport plan computed with the previous marginals, and permits zero weights despite dividing by those weights in the position update. The convexity statement in Section 4.2.2 applies to a fixed transport plan, not globally to the optimized transport objective.

The experiments do not convincingly isolate the claimed metric advantage. In Table 3, holding cross-entropy and per-class BatchNorm fixed, adding barycenter matching changes accuracy from 64.0% to 63.9%, 41.3% to 42.1%, and 37.4% to 37.9%. These results suggest modest, mixed incremental benefits. Section 5.5 removes augmentation and FKD differences but does not establish identical encoders and regularizers. Moreover, at one image per class, squared-Wasserstein matching targets the feature mean, just as linear-kernel MMD does; the large Table 4 gap cannot establish a geometric advantage without resolving these differences.

Baseline comparability is unresolved. Table 1 reports 21.3% for SRe2L on ImageNet-1K at 10 images per class, whereas the configuration identified as the baseline in Table 3 achieves 36.1%. Against the latter, the proposed method improves by 2.1 percentage points rather than 16.9. This discrepancy requires an explicit explanation and matched teacher, relabeling, and student-training protocols before the headline improvement can be interpreted reliably.

Important details needed to reproduce the central algorithm are missing from the supplied manuscript, including barycenter initialization, its iteration budget and learning rate, and the exact transport solver settings. Appendix E mainly specifies teacher training and image recovery, while subsequent training and relabeling details are delegated to SRe2L.

The efficiency evidence is too narrow for the scalability claims. Appendix F measures only ImageNette at one image per class, where the barycenter reduces to a mean and does not exercise the challenging multiple-support optimization. ImageNet-scale timings at larger image budgets, with costs separated for teacher training, feature extraction, transport optimization, and image recovery, are needed to substantiate the claimed small overhead.
